description: Baseline run of preprocessing sample detected 12 suspicious discovered people out of 161.

asi.hypothesis: Measure current junk rate before tightening discovered-person heuristics.
asi.benchmark: PREPROCESS_SAMPLE_ROWS=50000 with quality heuristic over dim_people discovered rows
asi.next_action_hint: Add stricter organization/newsletter/body-artifact filters before creating discovered people, then rerun the sample benchmark.

description: Tightened discovered-person display-name filtering to reject org/newsletter/body-artifact names, reducing suspicious discovered rows on the 50k sample.

asi.hypothesis: Most junk came from organization/newsletter-style display names slipping through discovery heuristics.
asi.what_changed: Expanded human_display_name_expr exclusions for org/news/body-artifact terms and numeric/octal-ish names.
asi.result: junk_people dropped from 12 to 2; discovered_people from 161 to 150; runtime slightly improved.
asi.next_action_hint: Investigate the remaining two and decide whether to add one more org-style exclusion or handle them as acceptable edge cases.

description: Filtered ampersand-bearing display names from discovered people, eliminating the last obvious organization-style false positive in the sample.

asi.hypothesis: The remaining junk was an org-style display name containing an ampersand, not a real person.
asi.what_changed: Rejected ampersand-bearing display names in human_display_name_expr in addition to org/news/body-artifact terms.
asi.result: junk_people dropped from 1 to 0 on the 50k sample; discovered_people slightly decreased to 148; runtime improved to 5.28s.
asi.tradeoff_note: This is a conservative recall hit for rare real human names with ampersands, but it removes the last obvious junk row in the sample.
asi.next_action_hint: If recall becomes an issue, consider a whitelist for genuinely human co-authored names instead of broad ampersand acceptance.

description: Rejected display names that look like mailbox-provider domain strings (e.g., '... gmail com'), but this did not improve junk_people on the benchmark sample.

asi.hypothesis: Some discovered junk slips through as normalized email-like names without '@'; rejecting mailbox-provider+TLD patterns should reduce that noise.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric unchanged at 0 junk_people on the target benchmark, so this tweak provides no measured improvement.
asi.next_action_hint: Stress-test with alternate sampling seeds to find residual junk not covered by the default seed and then target those patterns with minimal recall loss.
